plain_english_policy: This bill prohibits businesses, property owners, and employers in Alabama from creating policies that ban employees or visitors from transporting or storing firearms in their personal vehicles under specific conditions (e.g., the firearm is concealed/locked). It allows individuals who are injured by such bans to sue for damages. If an employee is fired for following these rules, they can get reinstated with back pay and benefits. The bill also limits liability for businesses if someone else's actions involving a gun cause harm, unless the business intentionally encouraged it.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would shift policy to protect individuals' rights to carry firearms in their vehicles while working or visiting properties that previously banned them under certain conditions. It creates new civil remedies (lawsuits for damages and reinstatement) against entities enforcing such bans, effectively mandating a more permissive stance on vehicle-borne firearm transport across private businesses and public/private employers.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Ford (Commerce and Small Business) advanced this bill to restrict employer/property owner policies against lawful vehicle firearm transport.
evidence_quotes: This bill would prohibit a business entity... from establishing policies against persons transporting or storing a firearm or ammunition when the person is otherwise in compliance with all other applicable laws under certain conditions.
A person who is injured or incurs damages, or the survivors of a person killed, as a result of a violation of subsection (b) may file a civil action...

An employee discharged by a public or private employer for a violation of a policy or rule prohibited by subsection (b) is entitled to full recovery... Reinstatement to the same position held at the time of his or her termination from employment, or to an equivalent position.
